stem: A 17-year-old boy has a dull ache in the left scrotum that worsens toward the end of the day. He has no fever or urinary symptoms. On standing, the left hemiscrotum looks fuller than the right, and the left testis itself feels normal and nontender.
oneliner: 17M + dull left scrotal ache worse by evening + no fever or urinary symptoms + left hemiscrotum fuller on standing + normal testis → which examination finding?

options.A: Mass that transilluminates and is unchanged by Valsalva maneuver
options.B: Bag of worms above the testis that grows with Valsalva
options.C: Tender, firm testis with an absent cremasteric reflex
options.D: Hard, painless nodule within the substance of the testis
options.E: Tender epididymis with pain relieved on lifting the testis

whyNot.A: Transillumination with **no change on Valsalva** is a **hydrocele or spermatocele**; his fullness appears on **standing**
whyNot.C: That is **testicular torsion**: acute severe pain; this boy has a chronic dull ache and a normal testis
whyNot.D: That suggests **testicular cancer**; his testis feels normal and the mass is **above** it
whyNot.E: Tender epididymis is **epididymitis**; his testis is **nontender** and he has **no fever or urinary symptoms**

answer: Soft, nontransilluminating mass above the testis that enlarges with Valsalva
why: A varicocele is a dilated **pampiniform plexus**, felt as a soft **bag of worms** above the testis. It **fills on standing or Valsalva** and empties lying down; it is usually **left-sided** because the left testicular vein enters the renal vein at a right angle.

idea.rule: Venous mass: fills when upright or straining, collapses when supine.
also: Left-sided because the left gonadal vein joins the renal vein
Right-sided or non-reducing varicocele: look for a retroperitoneal mass
Can reduce sperm quality and cause infertility
Renal tumor or left renal vein compression can cause a new left varicocele

stem: A 45-year-old man has had fever, chills, burning on urination and pain behind the scrotum for 2 days. He now passes urine in a weak, hesitant stream.
oneliner: 45M + 2 days fever, chills, dysuria, perineal pain + weak hesitant stream → which rectal examination finding?
ask: Which rectal examination finding is expected?

options.A: Diffusely enlarged, firm, smooth and nontender prostate
options.B: Hard, irregular, nodular area on the posterior lobe
options.C: Small, nontender prostate of normal consistency
options.E: Rubbery, nontender prostate with a midline cystic mass

whyNot.A: That is **BPH**; it is painless and he has **fever and chills**
whyNot.B: That is **prostate cancer**, which is hard and painless; he has an **acute febrile illness**
whyNot.C: A normal gland would not explain **fever, dysuria and perineal pain**
whyNot.E: A midline cyst is a **utricle or Müllerian remnant**, nontender and without fever

answer: Warm, boggy, very tender prostate (acute bacterial prostatitis)
why: Acute bacterial prostatitis causes **fever, chills, dysuria and perineal pain** with obstructive voiding from swelling. The inflamed gland is **warm, boggy and exquisitely tender**; massage is avoided because it can cause bacteremia.

idea.rule: Acute infection makes the gland tender; BPH and cancer are painless.
also: Prostate cancer: hard, nodular, asymmetric, usually posterior
Chronic prostatitis: mildly tender or normal
Common bugs: E. coli in older men, Chlamydia and gonorrhea in young men

stem: A 70-year-old man has had hesitancy, a weak stream, nocturia and dribbling after voiding for 2 years. He is afebrile and has no pain.
oneliner: 70M + 2 years hesitancy, weak stream, nocturia, postvoid dribbling + afebrile, no pain → which rectal examination finding?
ask: Which rectal examination finding is expected?

options.A: Diffusely enlarged, smooth, firm, nontender prostate
options.C: Hard, fixed, nodular posterior surface of the prostate
options.D: Tender fluctuant mass within the substance of the gland
options.E: Normal-sized gland with absent anal sphincter tone

whyNot.B: That is **acute prostatitis**; he is afebrile and has no pain
whyNot.C: Cancer arises in the **peripheral zone**, away from the urethra, so it rarely gives **slow outlet symptoms** like his; that gland feels hard and nodular
whyNot.D: That is a **prostatic abscess**: fever, severe pain and sepsis, none of which he has
whyNot.E: Absent tone points to a **cauda equina or cord lesion**, not slowly progressive outlet symptoms with a large gland

answer: Diffusely enlarged, smooth, firm, nontender prostate
why: BPH is hyperplasia of the **transition zone**, which squeezes the urethra and gives **hesitancy, weak stream, nocturia and postvoid dribbling**. On rectal exam the gland is **symmetrically enlarged, smooth, firm and nontender**.

idea.rule: Transition zone growth in older men gives smooth, painless enlargement.
also: Peripheral zone cancer feels hard and nodular
Acute prostatitis feels warm, boggy and tender
Transition zone surrounds the urethra, so outlet symptoms come early

stem: A 28-year-old woman finishing a course of antibiotics has vulvar itching and redness with a thick, white, curd-like vaginal discharge.
oneliner: 28F + recent antibiotics + vulvar itching and redness + thick white curdy discharge → which vaginal fluid finding?
ask: Which vaginal fluid finding is expected?

options.A: pH above 4.5, clue cells on saline, positive whiff test with KOH
options.B: pH above 4.5 with motile flagellated organisms on wet mount
options.C: pH 4.5 or less, pseudohyphae on KOH, negative whiff test
options.D: pH above 4.5 with many parabasal cells and few lactobacilli
options.E: Gram-negative diplococci inside neutrophils on Gram stain

whyNot.A: That is **bacterial vaginosis**: thin grayish discharge with a fishy odor, not itchy and curdy
whyNot.B: That is **trichomoniasis**: frothy yellow-green discharge, pH raised, motile trophozoites
whyNot.D: That is **atrophic vaginitis**: postmenopausal, low estrogen, not antibiotic-related and not curdy
whyNot.E: That is **gonorrhea** (cervicitis); it does not cause a thick curdy discharge or itching

answer: Normal pH with pseudohyphae on KOH and a negative whiff test
why: Antibiotics kill protective lactobacilli, allowing **Candida albicans** to overgrow with **curdy discharge and itching**. The vaginal **pH stays normal (4.5 or less)**, the whiff test is negative, and KOH shows **pseudohyphae**.

idea.rule: Yeast does not raise vaginal pH; bacteria and protozoa do.
also: Bacterial vaginosis: pH above 4.5, clue cells, positive whiff
Trichomonas: pH above 4.5, motile protozoa, strawberry cervix
Diabetes and pregnancy predispose to candidiasis
Treat with fluconazole or topical azoles

stem: A 10-year-old girl is seen for a well-child visit. A small mound of breast tissue is felt under an enlarged areola, and a few long, straight, lightly pigmented hairs are seen along the labia.
oneliner: 10F + small breast bud under enlarged areola + few long straight pale pubic hairs → which Tanner stage?
ask: Which Tanner stage does she match?

whyNot.A: Stage 1 is **prepubertal**: no breast bud, no pubic hair
whyNot.C: Stage 3 shows **breast and areola enlarging together** with darker, curlier pubic hair; she has only a few pale straight hairs
whyNot.D: Stage 4 has the **areola forming a secondary mound** and adult-type hair; hers has not
whyNot.E: Stage 5 is the **adult breast contour** with adult hair spreading to the thighs

answer: Tanner stage 2 (thelarche with sparse pubic hair)
why: Stage 2 is the **breast bud** under a **widened areola** (thelarche) with **sparse, long, lightly pigmented pubic hair** (pubarche). Breast budding is usually the **first sign of puberty** in girls, around age 10.

idea.rule: Girls: breast bud first (stage 2), then pubic hair, then menarche around stage 4.
also: Peak height velocity comes at about stage 3
Menarche follows about 2 years after thelarche
Boys: testicular enlargement is the first sign
Precocious puberty is breast development before age 8
